The public pilots page at https://www.saviours.xyz/pilots states that a run counts only when the operator is outside Saviour and a witness sees digest match
milestones.name: Reader and witness page

criteria: At least 1 team outside Saviour completes two audits of a mainnet Safe it governs that holds over $1 million and has Delay or Roles v2.1.1 enabled. A witness outside Saviour opens each pin link, the page shows digest match, and the pilots page names the team, the Safe, the block, the digest, and the balance query
milestones.name: First outside team

criteria: At least 4 further teams outside Saviour each complete two audits of a mainnet Safe they govern with Delay or Roles v2.1.1 enabled. Each of those Safes holds over $1 million, and at least 1 of the 5 teams holds over $50 million, with the address and the balance query linked on the pilots page. At least 3 teams are named there with the Safe, the block, and digest match. A witness outside Saviour opens each pin link and the page shows digest match. The technical reviewer confirms any unnamed team by seeing the Safe, the pin, and digest match, and the page states only the count

At least $2,500 of revenue, grants excluded, from those teams for a witnessed audit, with receipts the technical reviewer can check, and a public one-page plan of the hosted reader's monthly cost and how that cost is covered within 12 months
milestones.name: Five teams and upkeep

sections.commitments:
- The auditor stays under the MIT license already in the repo.
- Harshit Bainsla keeps the hosted reader up for 12 months after the last milestone, with no further ask to the fund.
- Pinned target: at least 5 outside teams, on the terms in the adoption milestones.
- Condition amounts stay unknown, Roles v1 is named and not interpreted, and the report never says the Safe is safe.
sections.in_scope:
- Bringing outside treasury teams onto the existing reader
- A public [pilots](https://www.saviours.xyz/pilots) page with the team or Safe, the block, the digest, the witness result, and the balance query
- Keeping [www.saviours.xyz/audit](https://www.saviours.xyz/audit) answering on Ethereum mainnet through the grant
- Charging those teams for a witnessed audit, and publishing a one-page plan of the hosted reader's monthly cost
sections.out_scope:
- Interpreting Roles v1, including the module in the 16 Nov 2026 incident
- Computing token amounts from Roles conditions or allowances
- A Safe App, or an import from the Safe Transaction Service
- Any chain other than Ethereum mainnet
- Detecting a compromised key, holding keys, or blocking a signature inside Safe
- The archived ENS naming product
sections.team:
**Harshit Bainsla** builds and maintains Saviour. The work is solo.

Track record: [github.com/devhb1/Saviour](https://github.com/devhb1/Saviour) and [www.saviours.xyz](https://www.saviours.xyz). The repo is MIT, copyright 2026 Harshit Bainsla.

[Kesavi Web Solutions](https://kesaviwebsolutions.com/) has committed $2,500, which is 25% of this goal. No other funder pays for this scope.
sections.why:
On 16 Nov 2026 a Safe lost about $6.45 million. [Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/safe-wallet-reportedly-loses-millions-after-key-compromise) put the transfer at about 4.39 million USDC and 1.72 million syrupUSDC, through a Zodiac Roles modifier, and quoted Zodiac's co-founder: the policy allowed the call, and the role member's key was most likely compromised. [Safe said no owner signed](https://coinmarketcap.com/academy/article/safe-multisig-zodiac-roles-key-compromise).

[Zodiac Roles](https://roles.gnosisguild.org) is where a team edits that policy. A co-signer still cannot hand someone a block-pinned link that a second person re-runs and matches.

Co-signers of mainnet Safes that use Delay or Roles v2.1.1 get that link. The page shows who can already act, and it leaves unread authority as unknown. The 16 Nov module is a Roles version this reader identifies and does not interpret. The loss shows the class of incident. This grant does not claim that loss would have been stopped.
sections.why_grant:
The reader is already on mainnet. Commit [`89f3902`](https://github.com/devhb1/Saviour/commit/89f3902) on [`main`](https://github.com/devhb1/Saviour) has the Safe and Delay reads, Roles v2.1.1 selectors from chain logs, a pin link whose digest ignores the RPC host, and a plain-language box that is dropped if it stamps the Safe as safe, invents a token amount, or claims a loss would have been prevented. The same read is on npm as [`@saviours/audit`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@saviours/audit).

A stranger can open [www.saviours.xyz/audit](https://www.saviours.xyz/audit) and the repo. One team proof, the Term Safe at block 26435999, is there so the read can be repeated. It does not count as an outside user.

The reader is built. This $10,000 pays for outside teams to use it, and for the hosted page to stay up.

initiative.summary: Saviour reads an Ethereum mainnet Safe at one block and reports who can act through it beyond the owners. The report covers the Safe, its Delay module, and Roles v2.1.1 members, targets, and selectors taken from chain logs. A second person opens the same link and checks that the digest matches. Condition amounts stay unknown, and the report never says the Safe is safe.
initiative.title: Saviour: Who can act through a Safe at one pinned block
